I will keep my land in the cropping pattern that fits Quzhou County best: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the system I would trust most because it matches the local climate, the local market, and the way I can manage risk with the knowledge and labor I have. I would not spread myself across too many crops. I would keep the plan simple, use improved seed, fertilize steadily instead of chasing very high input, irrigate at the key stages, and rely on a few timely pesticide sprays rather than many. For wheat, I would focus on strong establishment, spring fertilizer, and a few irrigations around jointing and grain filling. After wheat harvest, I would move quickly into summer maize, use no-tillage seeding to save time and moisture, then manage fertilizer, water, and weeds tightly because the maize season is short. I would choose this plan because it is the most dependable way for me to protect yield and keep the work manageable across the whole year.
